author: corsica
text: Hi Everyone My compression homework. From what I can understand Cps are a flagging area. In a bullish flag the cp will go down, consuming supply therefore making possible a move up on return. With a bearish flag you can see a CP going up while consuming demand, making it possible for the price to easily go down on return. That's why you will find poles and FLs on the left of a compressed area. Help and comments welcome!

author: staurum
text:
Hi Enlightenme, please see first the first post of this homework and have a good read on the Compression book (Red's work)

Ifmyante wrote: Compression is one of the most important signs that price is getting ready to turn.

As price is rising into Supply, it keeps dropping as it goes, filling the buy orders left at each Demand on the way up, allowing a quick drop through the CP zone when price hits Supply.

The exact opposite is true for Compression into Demand.

Here is a PDF about Compression www.readthemarket.com/media/pdf/Compression.pdf

Homework

Set up a subfolder for CP Homework and get into the charts

Find at least 20 CP setups, at HTF S/D zones, and explain what you see on each chart

Also chart the bigger picture where the CP occurred

While you're looking for CP, take the time to find at least 20 CPLQ (Liquidity) too

If you're not used to these, you can get stopped out of some fantastic trades and deeply regret not knowing why.

Your question: expect price to pass through? in any timeframe? What works or doesnot on CP-ed area is widely discussed here already. Price Action applies to all timeframes. If you have troubles understanding compression, Go over all the posts in this HW section, Pay attention to words/corrections made by the seniors here, and watch CP webinar by IF. Then you may start doing the HW instructions (pay attention too to the instructions). This will take time, please do not expect to grasp just by skimming and looking at the posts. Learning by doing is best.:)
